text:
olivia: Quick heads-up — proposing a small breaking change on /v1/generate. We want to replace the boolean query param compact_response with a response_format enum (values: compact, verbose, structured).

olivia: Current plan: deprecate compact_response on 2026-05-12 (warn header + logs), accept both for 4 weeks, then remove support on 2026-06-09. Need compatibility checklist and owners. :calendar:

mike: Will we auto-shim in the SDKs? Most clients use the SDK, but a lot of partners call REST directly.

olivia: Yes — SDKs will map compact_response=true -> response_format=compact automatically for one major release. But REST clients get a Deprecation header and a clear error after removal.

shaun: Can we keep the server accepting both during the window and emit a warning header so infra ops and partner teams can detect usage? Something like: 

  Deprecation: compact_response; sunset=2026-06-09
  Warning: 299 - "compact_response deprecated, use response_format"

shaun: Also we should log counts per-customer so CSMs can reach out.

anna: Docs update — I'll do the migration guide and a small code sample for curl + SDK. Timeline OK if I get final wording by 2026-04-30.

mike: Example snippets so folks know migration path: 

OLD: curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?compact_response=true" 
NEW: curl "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?response_format=compact"

mike: And server response shape changes? compact vs structured have slightly different envelopes. We need to be explicit.

olivia: compact keeps the short text string at top-level, verbose adds metadata (detokenization, timing), structured returns objects. We'll include sample responses in docs.

sarah: Heads-up — tests on integration env started failing when we tried the structured response in a feature branch. Gateway rejects unknown fields because some clients do strict schema checks. Propose a feature-flag gates for structured output rollout.

kevin: Another idea: add an opt-in header x-client-response-schema: "v1", "v1-compact", "v2-structured" so clients can declare what they expect. Server can honor or translate if possible. Could simplify compatibility and give us telemetry.

olivia: x-client-response-schema is interesting but risky — clients might not set it. I'd rather rely on Deprecation/Warning headers + server-side shim for compact->response_format for the deprecation window. But we can prototype x-client-response-schema as an experiment behind a flag.

shaun: For rollout we need: 
- infra: accept both params + emit warning header (owner: eng-runtime)
- telemetry: log usage per-customer and per-endpoint (owner: eng-platform analytics)
- sdk: map param + minor release (owner: devex)
- docs: migration guide + sample responses (owner: docs)
- partners: CSM outreach list (owner: customer-success)

mike: Who owns the canary and how do we measure regressions? I can set up a canary that flips structured on for 5% of internal traffic and monitor errors and latency.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-04-20 01:00 UTC (eng-runtime/canary-v2). Logs will be in /deploys/canary-v2.

anna: I'll prepare the docs PR to land on 2026-04-18. Slack announcement draft will be ready for review by EOD 2026-04-19.

kevin: Also add a lint rule in SDKs that warns if consumers are still using compact_response in code — small devex follow-up.

olivia: Action items: 
- eng-runtime: implement dual-accept + warning header and flag for structured (owner: shaun)
- eng-platform analytics: implement telemetry counts + dashboard (owner: mike)
- devex: SDK shim + lint rule (owner: kevin)
- docs & comms: migration guide + partner comms (owner: anna)
- customer-success: outreach list pulled from telemetry (owner: sarah)

olivia: Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree or add comments inline. We'll merge the plan tomorrow morning if no objections.
